answer: To stop sybils from sharing GPU hardware, agents audit peers using synchronized memory-bus saturation challenges. Challengers issue paired tasks, like rendering depth maps of a basalt mesa while completing a metered sonnet, under sub-millisecond deadlines. Because strict deadlines undercut kernel preemption and PCIe queue times, an attacker cannot multiplex weights across virtual nodes. Each identity requires dedicated VRAM and silicon, forcing sybil costs to scale linearly with real hardware.
